document.title: Andropov-Gromyko-Ustinov-Ponomarev Report to the CC CPSU on the Situation in Afghanistan, October 29, 1979
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan: Lessons from the Last War
document.note: Report on the situation in Afghanistan reflecting Soviet concerns about the regional impact of the Iranian revolution, perceived U.S. goals, and suspected Amin cooperation with American special services, adding to Soviet urgency.

events.description: Events in which Taraki was removed from power and then physically destroyed; Amin took power.
Recent plenum of the CC PDPA at which Amin promoted loyalists and relatives into ruling organs.
Andropov, Gromyko, Ustinov and Ponomarev submit report to CC CPSU recommending continued work with Amin while watching for an anti-Soviet turn.
Events of September 13-16 in which Taraki was removed from power and then physically destroyed; Amin consolidated power.

Planned execution of Politburo members Zerai, Misak, Pandzhshiri on fictitious charges, according to Soviet information.
Andropov, Gromyko, Ustinov and Ponomarev submit a report to the CC CPSU recommending continued work with Amin while guarding against his turn to the West.

key_claims: Taraki was removed and killed in the September 13-16, 1979 events, leaving Amin in power.
Amin widened repression in the Party, army, state apparatus and civic organizations despite superficial liberalizing gestures.
Soviet leaders reported that Amin planned to execute Politburo members Zerai, Misak and Pandzhshiri.
Amin promoted loyalists and relatives into the PDPA ruling organs.
Soviet leaders feared Amin would reorient toward the West and US representatives sensed such a shift.
The recommended Soviet line was to keep working with Amin while exposing his intentions and prepare supplemental measures if he turned anti-Soviet.
